name: Lazarus RipperDoc Street Clinic Full Rig
description:
Street ripperdoc's complete working set: a long-sleeved antimicrobial wrap-coat in deep teal with brown burn-stains that no amount of washing removes, over a sealed nitrile underlayer. Surgical cap is recycled poly-weave, ear loops reinforced with wire to accommodate horn or fin geneware. Face shield is scratched but intact. Apron front has tiered tool loops — scalpels, probe leads, cable management clips.

Feet: sealed boot-covers over heavy rubber-soled work boots, non-slip tread. Gloves are double-layered — inner BCI-conductive, outer disposable nitrile. The whole rig smells faintly of isopropyl and ozone. Nothing matches. Everything functions.
functionality: Antimicrobial outer layer, BCI-conductive inner gloves for interface during surgery, sealed nitrile underlayer for biohazard protection, tool-loop apron, non-slip boot covers, gene-compatible surgical cap with reinforced loops.
what_it_says: This person fixes what the licensed clinics won't touch, for people who can't afford to ask questions.
story_hooks: The burn stains on the coat are not from surgery — the ripperdoc won't say what caused them.
The BCI-conductive gloves are a licensed Lazarus model, far too expensive for a Shelf clinic — someone is supplying this doc.
A patient recognizes the tool-loop apron's stitching pattern as belonging to a Tier-4 surgical suite that went dark six months ago.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, layered silhouette built for function over fashion. The long wrap-coat dominates, with a slightly oversized, unstructured drape that moves with the wearer's body. The tiered apron front creates visual weight and practical geometry. Overall impression: a working medic, not a surgeon with a sterile suite. Deliberately unglamorous.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and intentionally oversized through the torso for mobility and layering. The wrap-coat cinches at the waist with loose ties rather than buttons, allowing quick removal or adjustment. Sleeves are long and loose enough to roll when needed. Underlayer and boot-covers create a sealed, contained look from neck to ankle.
physical_description.primary_material: Wrap-coat: treated synthetic-wool blend with chemical-resistant coating. Underlayer: medical-grade sealed nitrile. Surgical cap: recycled poly-weave with reinforced ear loops. Apron: woven nylon with stitched tool loops. Gloves: dual-layer (BCI-conductive inner, disposable nitrile outer). Boot-covers: sealed rubber compound.
physical_description.texture: Stained and deliberately worn. The wrap-coat shows permanent brown burn marks and isopropyl discoloration that have become part of the surface. Nitrile has a subtle sheen and slight tackiness. Tool loops are reinforced with visible stitching. Gloves have a matte finish with faint powdering. Boot-covers are textured rubber with deep tread marks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep teal wrap-coat as dominant color, with persistent brown staining across the front and sleeves. Cream-white nitrile underlayer visible at the neckline. Black surgical cap, clear face shield (with visible scratch marks), natural rubber boot-covers. Metallic accents from wire reinforcements and tool clips.
physical_description.closures: Wrap-coat fastens with loose fabric ties at the waist—no buttons, no zippers, designed for quick access and removal. Nitrile underlayer uses friction-fit. Surgical cap has reinforced elastic ear loops with embedded wire. Boot-covers slip on with friction and elasticated cuffs. Gloves are pull-on with no closure.
distinctive_features: Tiered apron front with asymmetrical tool loops sized for surgical instruments, probe leads, and cable management
Permanent brown burn-stains that mark the wrap-coat as authentically used in high-heat interventions
Wire-reinforced ear loops on surgical cap, designed to accommodate geneware (horns, fins, or modified ears)
Scratched but intact clear face shield, showing signs of regular use and minor chemical splash
Double-layered gloves: BCI-conductive inner layer for direct nerve interfacing with augmentations
Heavy rubber-soled boots with non-slip deep tread, visible through transparent boot-covers
Completely mismatched aesthetic—nothing was chosen for style, everything for durability and function
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 indicator. This is working-class street medicine gear, not corpo-certified equipment. The wear patterns and cost-effective materials signal someone operating outside official medical infrastructure.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is the uniform of a ripperdoc—an illegal or semi-legal augmentation specialist who works from street clinics in the ungoverned zones. Wearing this rig signals technical skill, willingness to operate in gray markets, and proximity to underground modification culture. It says: 'I can crack your nervous system open and rewire it, and I don't need a sterile corporate facility to do it.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually weathered and stained. The burn marks are permanent. The face shield is always scratched. The apron carries faint residue from a dozen different procedures. Nothing is pristine; everything is functional. The whole rig carries the faint chemical smell of isopropyl and ozone—a smell that never quite washes out.
